Mood Board

1,220 sq ft · 2 bed / 3 bath

Style: Transitional — black-and-white checkerboard floors and matte black hardware throughout, with clean-lined fixtures over rustic ones and the living room's olive green sleeper sofa as a deliberate pop of color. Baths repeat the look in sea-glass tile with black grout over dark floors.

A full remodel: kitchen, dining, and living refreshed in place; both bedrooms and their ensuites rebuilt; the downstairs half bath upgraded to a full curbless wet room; new closets, stairs, and hardware throughout. Layout changes stay minor — a 6" wall shift for the half bath's shower and toilet, opened walls between the primary closets, and a resized tub with a respaced vanity in the primary bath.

Colors

Leona checkerboard tile is the throughline across every main room, paired with reclaimed hardwood on the stairs and landings (Special Walnut-stained); wet zones — entryways and all three baths — switch to Dawson's charcoal tile underfoot, with Lilah, Opal — a glossy, sea-glass-look wall tile run floor-to-ceiling with black grout — and matte black fixtures and hardware throughout.

By Room
Primary Bedroom Primary Bathroom

A shared kids' room built for privacy and symmetry: twin beds flank the window, both headed to the bottom wall and flush to their own side wall, each with a Thuma Floating Side Table rail-clamped to its own frame, and a ceiling-hung curtain, 40" long, hangs from each headboard wall to cut light pollution between the two. A 36"x60" Model Railroad Workbench table sits flush against the top wall, on the right side of the hallway to the bathroom, with Kato's own published "Cheap & Nothing Wasted II" N-scale track plan superimposed on top, semi-transparent, as a real reference image. Walk-in closets with more privacy curtains, cabinets, desktops, mirrors.

Secondary Bedroom Secondary Bathroom

A standalone bedroom — Twin bed tucked into the corner with a Thuma Floating Side Table, desk and chair in the old closet nook flanked by matching floor-to-ceiling built-in organizers. Its en-suite has a curbless tiled shower (fixed glass panel + curtain, ceiling rainhead, no threshold), a TOTO UltraMax WASHLET+ toilet, a 24" West Elm Mid-Century Open Storage vanity, Acorn, and Edward Martin Lilah, Opal tile on all four walls over a Dawson, Charcoal floor.

Kitchen Dining Room Living Room Entryway Stairs

No changes to the kitchen's white cabinetry, stainless appliances, granite counters, or backsplash. Two counter stools at the island; the dining desk stations use low chairs instead. New kitchen window treatment.

Counters continue from the kitchen, dropped to table height. 48" round marble table seats 4-6 (6 chairs shared between dining table and computer stations). Bi-fold door to the patio.

Power-recline sleeper sofa faces the built-in entertainment center, which stays as-is.

Archway passage between living room and kitchen with a wall-hung arched mirror.

Reclaimed hardwood treads lead to the upstairs bedroom suites, paired with a rust-toned tile riser for contrast; the second landing and the near half of the top landing continue that same hardwood, while the rest of the top landing, outside the bedroom door, is straight-set Leona Nero.

Main floor plan to scale — living room 171"x169", kitchen and dining room each 137"x137". Downstairs bath shown schematically; see its own plan.

Scope of Workappendix A — what's included, room by room

A full remodel, scoped and priced room by room so any firm walking the house bids exactly this list — no assumed extras outside what's written below. Brands, SKUs, and specific products are listed in Appendix B; this list is deliberately just the categories of work being asked for.

Whole House
  • New tile flooring throughout, hardwood stairs
  • Whole-house paint, including ceilings and select built-ins
  • New tile baseboard trim throughout (stairs get neither — a stairwell doesn't normally get one)
  • Suggested tiles called out, paint colors per designer
Entry + Hallway
  • New floor tile
  • New light fixture and entry mirror
Kitchen
  • New floor tile
  • New window coverings
  • Existing cabinets, counters, and appliances stay as-is
Dining Room
  • Remove slider, new bi-fold patio door
  • New table-height base cabinets with counter, two desk stations
  • New floor tile, new outlets at the desk stations
  • New window coverings
Living Room
  • New ceiling light fixture
  • New floor tile
  • Repaint the existing built-in entertainment center
  • New window coverings
Primary Bedroom
  • Remove existing closet walls, rebuild walk-in closet layout
  • New floor tile, bedroom and both walk-in closets
  • Built-in closet organizer systems, both closets
  • New closet mirrors, closet curtains, and ceiling bed curtains
  • New lighting, new window coverings
Primary Bathroom
  • Reconfigure entry to a pocket door
  • New tub/shower, new vanity, new toilet, new fixtures throughout
  • New floor and wall tile
  • New lighting and medicine cabinet
Secondary Bedroom
  • Remove reach-in closet walls, expand the room into the closet — new framing to achieve
  • New floor tile
  • Built-in organizers flanking the bed
  • New window coverings
Secondary Bathroom
  • New curbless shower, new vanity, new toilet, new fixtures (en-suite, new construction)
  • New floor and wall tile
  • New lighting and medicine cabinet
Downstairs Bathroom
  • Reframe to fit a curbless corner shower; new pocket door
  • Bump out a wall 6" toward front entry for additional floor space
  • New wall-mount corner sink with mirrors, new toilet, new fixtures
  • New floor-to-ceiling wall tile and new floor tile
  • New lighting
Under-Stairs Closet
  • Convert to a clothes wardrobe: shelving/rod, counter, vanity mirror, lighting
  • New floor tile, new curtain in place of the door
Stairs
  • New reclaimed hardwood tread
  • New riser tile
  • New landing flooring
Furniture
  • New furniture package throughout — both bedrooms, dining, living room, and accent pieces
  • Tracked and priced separately from the construction scope above
